done_when: Approving a candidate-backed memory review saves the memory; the review card reports the real outcome (approved, failed with reason, or already decided); a Postgres test covers approving a candidate-backed review end to end

findings.body: The Postgres test calls `service.decideReview` directly, bypassing the user-facing approval entry point and card update. The new card tests mock the internal IPC decision and subject lookup (`apps/core/test/unit/bootstrap/approving-a-learned-memory-always-fails.test.ts:5`), so they cannot prove that real database outcomes reach the card. Actual Slack card replacement occurs in `apps/core/src/channels/slack/channel-message-action-handler.ts:263`, which neither test exercises. Add the required end-to-end flow through the running application with real Postgres, verifying saved memory and visible approved, failed-with-reason, and already-decided outcomes; fake only third-party edges. The current coverage does not satisfy the explicit Done-when test requirement.
findings.title: Not done: Candidate-backed approval and review-card outcomes need end-to-end coverage

why: Approving a learned memory always fails as stale while the card still says 'Memory review approved', so preferences and corrections can never be approved
